title: Immigration strategy endorsed amid federal funding cuts
subtitle: A resident raised smoke-free housing enforcement concerns, and the committee agreed to join an All Councils meeting on June 13.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that Regional Council endorse the Waterloo Region Immigration Strategy 2025-2028 and commit to supporting the economic and social success of immigrants, including advocating for federal and provincial policy and investment {{vote:m1}}. The strategy was developed by the Immigration Partnership, which brings together more than 70 partner organizations.

Presenters said the partnership is operating with reduced federal funding and is seeking other sources. Staff and the Regional Chair noted that earlier advocacy to federal representatives did not reverse the cut. Councillors spoke in support, and one invited the partnership to present to each area municipality.

A resident delegate raised concerns about enforcement of smoking rules and the Region's Smoke-Free Housing policy at a seniors building in Wellesley. The committee asked staff to meet with the delegate about current smoking laws and possible remedies. The committee also recommended that Council take part in an All Councils meeting on June 13 {{vote:m2}}. The next committee meeting is August 12, 2025.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse the community-developed Waterloo Region Immigration Strategy 2025-2028, commit to leadership in supporting immigrants' economic and social success, and advocate for federal and provincial policy and investment.
The committee recommended that the Region participate in an All Councils meeting on June 13, 2025 at 2:30 p.m. at 150 Frederick Street, Kitchener.

debate: A delegate said the Region's smoke-free housing policy is not consistently enforced. They pointed to differing smoking-distance signs across locations and asked for a 20-metre distance and timely enforcement near seniors' non-smoking buildings.

Two councillors asked staff to refresh Council on the smoking by-law and its limits. One said provincial legislation may limit making older buildings non-smoking. Staff from by-law and Waterloo Regional Housing agreed to meet the delegate.

Presenters said the Immigration Partnership faces a significant funding gap over the next three years. They described a funding subcommittee looking at philanthropic, private and public sources, and said provincial funding that once supported the work was withdrawn in 2021-22.

A councillor asked about provincial funding and whether the issue could be raised at AMO in August. The Regional Chair said the Region had lobbied federal representatives without success and would keep partnering with the Immigration Partnership.

Asked about area municipalities, the presenters said they have not given direct funding, but municipal staff contribute time and expertise. One councillor said that time is paid for by the municipality and invited the partnership to present to their council.
